source.title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data

confidence_rationale: Shumailov et al. give a rigorous, general demonstration -- theoretical plus empirical across LLMs, VAEs, and Gaussian mixture models -- that indiscriminately training a generative model on its own (or a related model's) generated output causes 'model collapse': tails of the true distribution disappear and errors compound across generations, an effect they show is close to inevitable without deliberate countermeasures. This directly corroborates the load-bearing anti-circularity requirement MECH-514 registers: 'repeated simulations derived from one episode must not become multiple independent samples,' and the raw thought's own framing that 'the central danger is that material generated or interpreted through the attractor is counted as independent evidence for it.' Model collapse is the demonstrated failure mode when that discipline is absent at the scale of generative-model training; MECH-514 proposes the analogous discipline (provenance-tagging every replay-derived item, requiring some independence in what gets selected for replay) at the scale of one system's offline counterfactual replay. The paper does not test MECH-514's specific protocol (bounded alternative-model construction, held-out validation before granting reindexing authority) -- it establishes the generic hazard MECH-514's anti-pseudo-replication requirement exists to prevent, at one remove.
failure_signatures: Model collapse is demonstrated for generative models trained across successive generations/iterations on self-generated data at population/corpus scale (LLMs, VAEs, GMMs); MECH-514's anti-circularity concern is about a single system's own online-vs-replay bookkeeping within one memory/inference cycle, a different granularity than multi-generation training collapse.

The paper's countermeasure discussion centres on preserving access to genuine, human-generated data as generated content proliferates online; it does not propose or test a provenance-tagging / replay-selector-independence mechanism of the specific kind MECH-514 requires.

No neuroscience or hippocampal-replay content: this is a pure ML/statistics paper about training-data composition over generations, with no claim about biological memory consolidation or offline replay.

mapping.source_claim_statement: When a generative model's own output (or output from other generative models) is fed back into training data without discrimination from genuinely-sourced data, the resulting models suffer 'model collapse': low-probability tail events and rare-but-real distributional features are progressively lost across generations (early collapse), and this can proceed to near-total loss of diversity (late collapse). The authors show this occurs theoretically and empirically across large language models, variational autoencoders, and Gaussian mixture models, and argue it is close to an inevitable long-term consequence unless the provenance of training data (human-generated vs. model-generated) is tracked and managed.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-514's anti-pseudo-replication requirement is the same hazard restated at the scale of a single cognitive architecture's memory rather than a training corpus: if replay-derived content (simulations generated by running evidence through the dominant or alternative explanatory models) is not provenance-tagged back to its originating evidence and generating model, repeated simulations from one episode can be miscounted as multiple independent confirming samples -- functionally the same 'feeding your own generated content back in as if it were new ground truth' error that drives model collapse, just occurring within one system's replay loop rather than across successive training runs of a population of models. Shumailov et al. give strong, general grounds for treating this as a real and serious hazard class rather than a remote theoretical worry, which supports MECH-514's decision to make provenance-tagging and replay-selector independence load-bearing requirements rather than optional refinements.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is evidence for the generic hazard class (self-generated content miscounted as independent evidence degrades a system over repeated cycles), not a direct test of MECH-514's specific offline counterfactual-replay protocol. The paper's unit of collapse is a population of models trained across generations on a shared, increasingly synthetic corpus; MECH-514's unit is a single system's replay-derived items within one memory/inference cycle. The transfer from 'generative model pretraining corpus contamination' to 'attractor-replay pseudo-replication inside one cognitive architecture' is a domain-general-principle transfer, not a same-substrate replication, and should be read as motivating MECH-514's requirement rather than validating its implementation.
mapping.source_context: High-profile peer-reviewed Nature paper (2024) combining theoretical analysis with empirical demonstrations across three distinct model classes (LLMs, VAEs, GMMs); widely cited and treated as a foundational reference for the 'model collapse' / synthetic-data-contamination literature in ML.

confidence_components.notes: Very high source quality -- a Nature paper combining theory and cross-architecture empirical demonstration of a now-foundational ML phenomenon. Mapping fidelity is moderate: the underlying principle (self-generated content miscounted as independent evidence degrades a system) transfers cleanly in the abstract, but the paper's unit of analysis (multi-generation corpus contamination across a population of trained models) is structurally different from MECH-514's unit (provenance-tagged replay items within one system's offline counterfactual protocol). Transfer risk is moderate: this is a domain-general-principle transfer rather than a same-substrate test, so it is read as motivating evidence for the anti-circularity requirement rather than validation of MECH-514's specific mechanism.
